title: Issued USGS aftershock forecasts for 248 mainshocks (2019-2026) were calibrated after Bayesian updates at depths to 70 km but too high for deeper mainshocks and Guam-Marianas 10 km circles
abstract: Question: are the aftershock forecasts that the USGS Operational Aftershock Forecast (OAF) system issued calibrated, and which archived model variant scores best? Approach: we downloaded all 14,437 issued OAF versions in ComCat for 252 mainshocks (M 3.8-8.8, 2019-2026; mostly the automated system from late 2024). We counted ComCat earthquakes in each stated search circle for windows of 1 day to 1 year that ended by 2026-11-01. We scored the probability of 1 or more events at magnitudes at or above the completeness magnitude that OAF used. We wrote the plan before scoring and bootstrapped by mainshock. Results: the first issued versions (median 10 minutes after the origin, mostly generic) gave 190 windows with events against 310 expected (O/E 0.61, 95% CI 0.47-0.75). Over all versions, mainshocks at depths to 70 km gave O/E 0.97 (0.84-1.10), with a reliability curve near the diagonal. For the same units, archived generic forecasts gave O/E 0.63, sequence-specific 1.02 and Bayesian (issued) 0.97; the Bayesian variant had the best Brier and log scores. The 31 mainshocks deeper than 70 km gave 45 against 294 (O/E 0.15) and 0 against 35 in 1-day windows; they received shallow subduction-zone generic parameters. Guam-Marianas mainshocks at depths to 70 km gave 12 against 161 in 10 km circles. In a post-hoc check with circles 3 times wider, the Guam-Marianas 1-day and 1-week ratios rose to about 1, but the deep 1-day ratio stayed at 0.09. Versions issued more than 90 days after the mainshock were too low (O/E 1.41). Limitations: the result depends on the counting circle and on the final ComCat catalog; groups for deep events, M 7+ bins and larger-than-mainshock events are small; we could not compare ETAS with RJ for the same units.
